findings.problem: TODO comment asserts 'use Rayon and SmallVec because it will be faster' with zero measurement, baseline, workload description, or target-hardware context.
findings.failure_mode: Rayon task-scheduling overhead on a 4-element input will massively dominate computation time, producing measurable slowdown rather than speedup; SmallVec inline-capacity-4 avoids heap allocation but does not address whether an array return is even needed.
findings.fix: Remove the claim. Measure with a benchmark comparing current Vec collect vs [String; 4] or caller-owned buffer vs SmallVec<4>. No optimization without baseline.

findings.problem: Proposing Rayon for 4-element input. Rayon dispatch overhead (thread pool scheduling, work-stealing, result collection) is orders of magnitude larger than the 4 iterations of a bitwise AND and string lookup.
findings.failure_mode: Throughput degrades measurably under Rayon for inputs of size 4; the parallelism benefit never materializes because each task's work is ~2 CPU cycles while pool dispatch costs thousands.
findings.fix: Never use Rayon for inputs at or below ~100 elements. This is a fixed-4 API — use a manual unrolled loop or iterator; no parallelism needed.

findings.problem: Function returns `Vec<&'static str>` for a guaranteed 4-element input, causing at least one heap allocation per call. The output size is statically known.
findings.failure_mode: Every call allocates on the heap for 4 pointer-sized elements. A `[&'static str; 4]` return or caller-owned buffer eliminates allocation entirely with zero complexity tradeoff.
findings.fix: Change return type to `[&'static str; 4]` and populate with a bounded loop or unrolled assignments. Only use SmallVec<ArrayVec> if the size distribution justifies it per SKILL.md line 71.

findings.problem: No benchmark module exists anywhere in the crate. The TODO makes a performance claim without any `[bench]` section in Cargo.toml, no criterion/nightly benchmark, and no baseline numbers.
findings.failure_mode: Optimization direction is guessed, not measured. The actual bottleneck (if any) may be downstream consumers, not this function. Any change is blind.
findings.fix: Add a criterion benchmark or minimal `test`-attribute baseline comparing current Vec vs fixed-array return. Report workload, command, number, and hardware in final claims.

findings.problem: TODO marker signals an unexecuted intent. The SKILL.md requires that claimed performance work be supported by actual command evidence, not planned work.
findings.failure_mode: Future implementation may follow the folklore path (Rayon + SmallVec) without measurement, embedding the wrong optimization into production code.
findings.fix: Replace the TODO with a measured observation or remove it until benchmark data exists.

missing_evidence: no benchmark module or benchmark command in crate
no baseline performance number for the current Vec implementation
no profiler output (flamegraph, perf, or equivalent)
no allocation measurement (e.g., allocs/call from criterion or similar)
no second-ring evidence comparing [T; 4] vs Vec vs SmallVec<4>
no CLI command evidence for any performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code is safe (no unsafe/panic/unwrap) and functionally correct, but the folklore performance TODO introduces a high risk of anti-pattern implementation (Rayon on 4 elements, premature SmallVec adoption) without measurement. The unnecessary Vec allocation on fixed-size output is the highest-confidence defect.
